To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an effective model of our HPGe detector and used it to measure the background of a rock sample from the INO site.
we have characterized a HPGe detector and made an effective model of the same using Monte Carlo simulations.
we have made an effective detector model for the TIFR HPGe detector and have estimated the radio-purity levels of the rock sample from INO site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, characterization, and simulation of the low background HPGe detection system.
the design, development and characterization of a low background counting setup and its applications in the field of rare event searches.
development of techniques for low background experiments, and the characterization of a HPGe detector for such experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the background of the HPGe detector is dominated by the internal radioactivity of the HPGe crystal itself, which is in the order of 0.1-0.2 counts/keV/kg/day.
the HPGe setup is a reliable, low background and efficient counting setup for the measurement of radioactivity.
the setup and the analysis method are working well and are ready to be used for the INO site characterization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have characterized the detector and its response to different sources and have made an effective detector model using Geant4 simulations.
the setup is capable of measuring radio-impurities at the 10-17g/kg level.
we have characterized the detector response to various sources, developed a GEANT4 based model of the detector, and estimated radio-impurities at INO site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a detailed characterization of the detector is important in the context of rare event searches.
a low activity copper + lead shield is sufficient to reduce the background in a HPGe detector to the level of 10-20 mBq/kg in the energy range 2-10 MeV.
the background from a rock sample at INO site can be reduced to the level of a few events/tonne/year.
